# Test fixture provenance

Every `.wav` fixture is generated by `generate-au0.py`, run out of process:

```sh
uv run --no-project --with soundfile==0.12.1 --with numpy==2.1.3 \
    python -I tests/fixtures/generate-au0.py
```

The 16-bit files come from Python's standard-library `wave` module (PSF-2.0) or from [soundfile](https://github.com/bastibe/python-soundfile) 0.12.1 (BSD-3-Clause). soundfile wraps libsndfile 1.2.0 (LGPL-2.1), which only runs in that separate process. The sample values are synthetic test data written for this repo (MIT), made by the same 31-bit LCG as `tests/package.lisp`. The writers are only oracles. Regenerate the fixtures rather than hand-edit them. The generator reads every file back with soundfile, and the 16-bit ones with `wave` too, and stops if a file doesn't give back the codes it wrote.

| File | What | Writer |
|------|------|--------|
| `wave-pcm16-mono.wav` | 8000 Hz, 1 channel, 64 frames, including -32768 and 32767 | `wave` |
| `wave-pcm16-stereo.wav` | 22050 Hz, 2 channels, 50 frames | `wave` |
| `sf-pcm16-stereo.wav` | 44100 Hz, 2 channels, 40 frames | soundfile, `WAV` / `PCM_16` |
| `sf-pcm24-mono-odd.wav` | 48000 Hz, 1 channel, 33 frames: 99 data bytes, then a pad byte | soundfile, `WAV` / `PCM_24` |
| `sf-pcm24-stereo.wav` | 96000 Hz, 2 channels, 20 frames | soundfile, `WAV` / `PCM_24` |
| `sf-float32-stereo.wav` | 16000 Hz, 2 channels, 30 frames, including -0.0, 1.5, -2.0 and a subnormal; libsndfile adds `fact` and `PEAK` chunks | soundfile, `WAV` / `FLOAT` |
| `sf-pcm16-info.wav` | 11025 Hz, 1 channel, 21 frames, a `LIST`/`INFO` chunk (title, artist) before `data` | soundfile, `WAV` / `PCM_16` |
| `sf-pcm16-wavex.wav` | WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, 32000 Hz, 2 channels, 15 frames, `fact` chunk | soundfile, `WAVEX` / `PCM_16` |
| `sf-pcm24-wavex-3ch.wav` | WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, 44100 Hz, 3 channels, 12 frames | soundfile, `WAVEX` / `PCM_24` |
| `sf-float32-wavex.wav` | WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, 8000 Hz, 1 channel, 25 frames, `fact` and `PEAK` | soundfile, `WAVEX` / `FLOAT` |
| `au0-files.sexp` | For each `.wav` above: encoding, rate, channels, frames and every sample code, as soundfile reads the file back | soundfile |

Codes: a 16-bit or 24-bit sample is its signed integer. A float32 sample is the unsigned 32-bit integer of its IEEE bits, so the comparison is exact.

## Where the writers differ from `write-wav`

- libsndfile writes float32 files with a 16-byte `fmt` chunk, then `fact` and `PEAK`. `write-wav` writes the 18-byte `fmt` chunk (cbSize 0) that the WAVEFORMATEX spec asks for non-PCM data, then `fact`. So float files are compared by value, not byte for byte.
- libsndfile converts floats to 16-bit codes with a scale of 32767. `write-wav` uses 32768, the inverse of reading, so a file read and written back keeps its codes. The live cross-read compares codes and never asks libsndfile to convert.
